newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banking sector 1996 net jumps 30.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish banking sector 1996 net jumps 30.2 pct.

text.p: The net profit of the Polish banking sector last year jumped 30.2 percent in real terms against 1995 to 4.45 billion zlotys, the National Bank of Poland's President Hanna Gronkiewcz-Waltz said on Monday.
She said the growth of profits of the whole sector was a result of improved financial results of all types of banks -- foreign-controlled and Polish commercial banks as well as cooperative banks.
"The banking system as a whole is well and 1996 was another year of improved results of both commercial and cooperative banks," Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a news conference.

The banking sector's gross profit grew 17.5 percent in real terms against 1995 to 6.61 billion zlotys on total revenues of 33.30 billion, down 3.1 percent in real terms and total costs of 26.69 billion, 7.2 percent lower than in 1995 in real terms.
"The better results are due to the implementation of better safety regulations such as provisions for irregular loans and better management," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.
Banks controlled by foreign capital again led the sector in terms of performance, recording a net profit jump of 305.1 percent in nominal terms against 1995 to 615.8 million zlotys.
The net profit of cooperative banks, long in the red, also jumped 121.4 percent in nominal terms to 192.2 million zlotys.
Groniewicz-Waltz said the net profit margin of the banking sector grew to 16.7 percent in 1996 against 11.9 in 1995 while the gross profit margin rose to 24.8 percent from 19.6 percent.

Polish commercial banks had the highest net profit margin of the whole sector at between 18.1 and 18.3 percent in 1996 against 4.3-16.0 percent in 1995 while foreign-owned banks had 16.4 percent last year against 15 percent in 1995.
Cooperative banks increased their net profit margin in 1996 to 11.8 percent against 5.6 percent in 1995.

The sector's gross return on assets rose 0.14 point to 3.32 and their net return on assets rose 0.16 point to 1.8 percent in 1996 while the gross return on equity rose 2.3 point to 26.38 percent and net return on equity rose 1.16 point to 17.57 percent.
The banking sector's balance sheet total rose 12.1 percent in real terms to 198.34 billion zlotys.
Banks' credit portfolio improved in 1996 as the amount of bad loans in the sector dropped by 7.9 points to 12.5 percent of gross credits.

Despite the sale of stakes in banks in 1996 the treasury increased its holdings in the banking sector's share capital by 3.89 percent to 41.53 percent as a result of a capital rise of Bank Zachodni, Pekao SA and the buying of Bank Staropolski SA.
Foreign banks increased their stake in the sector's capital to 29.79 percent in 1996 from 19.24 percent in 1995, and the central bank reduced its stake to 7.87 percent from 8.9 percent.
Poland has two state-owned banks which do not operate under the commercial code, 79 commercial banks which are joint-stock companies and 1,394 cooperative banks.
